newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures failed to hang on to their early gains after a cut in call money and drifted lower in a lacklustre session to test Friday's lows.

Traders said the session had been calm and that the contract looked set to be stuck in a range this week with little on the economic calendar to excite much interest although the tone remained bullish.
"The beast is sleeping ... I fear the rest of the week will be like Monday in the absence of major news," said the head trader at a French brokerage.

The December bond contract climbed to a high of 126.56 soon after the open, failed to add to its gains after the German M3 release which was in line with expectations, then slipped to settle at 126.32.

The trader said he expected the contract to trade between 126.28/34 and 126.70/80 for the rest of the week. Another trader said he expected the contract to remain between 125.60, the low of the past two weeks, and 126.60, last week's high.
Economists said the cut in call money would boost expectations for a cut in the intervention rate at the Bank of France's next policy meeting on October 31.
Although a lowering in call money had been expected at some stage, PIBOR contracts were bolstered by the cut in the overninght rate to 3-1/4 3/8 percent on Monday.
December PIBOR set a contract high at 96.47 before slipping to settle at 96.43. It outperformed December Euromarks with the spread narrowing to 42 basis points from 44.
"The spread between (call money) and the floor rate is now only six basis points, a signal that the intervention rate will be cut sometime," said Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley in Paris.

Economists said the proximity of the overnight rate to the intervention rate, which sets the floor for French money market rates, meant the intervention rate would be cut soon while the recent strength of the franc provided a favourable backdrop.

"They're at the point where they have to consider cutting the intervention rate," said Philippe Brossard, head of reserach at ABN Amro in Paris. He said a 10 basis point cut on October 31 was a possibility even if German rates were left unchanged.
Chaney also said, "I still favour the end of October monetary policy council meeting as a likely date for a 10 basis point cut."
Traders said there had been little action in the cash market on Monday and 10-year OATs lost ground against their German counterparts.
The yield on the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT rose to 5.95 percent from 5.94 and the spread over the April 2006 Bunds moved to minus two from minus five basis points.
The franc slipped as low as 3.3806 per mark from 3.3767 late on Friday.
